claims.text: The high-entropy alloy has a naturally formed protective oxide film.
Controlled sliding wear in a corrosive environment disrupts or removes the protective oxide film.
Repeated mechanical disruption prevents the oxide film from repassivating sufficiently quickly.
Oxide-film disruption exposes fresh alloy surface.
Exposure of fresh alloy surface accelerates corrosion.
Corrosion reduces the alloy's resistance to wear.
Mutual reinforcement between oxide removal, corrosion, and reduced wear resistance intensifies overall degradation.
Total degradation during simultaneous tribo-corrosion will exceed the arithmetic sum of degradation measured during isolated wear and isolated corrosion.
Wear-scar metrics during tribo-corrosion will be elevated relative to isolated-wear baseline measurements.
Corrosion indicators such as corrosion current density will be elevated during tribo-corrosion relative to isolated-corrosion baseline measurements.
The predicted synergy should hold when a protective oxide forms but cannot repassivate quickly enough to offset repeated mechanical disruption.
The predicted synergy may fail for alloys with extremely rapid repassivation.
The predicted synergy may fail in environments where passivation is thermodynamically impeded.
The magnitude of synergistic degradation may depend on alloy composition and repassivation kinetics.
